ground_truth.reason: This PR includes the feature with the fix already applied, so the vulnerability is not present

fix_commit_message:
* src/sdf/ftsdf.c (sdf_generate_bounding_box): Fix thinko.

Bug introduced in commit bda1d87f694dd.

We would need an `FT_NEW_ARRAY_MULT` array...

Reported as

  https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/494362618
agent_reasoning: Merged diff composed mechanically by cherry-picking fix 4130e62d2348 on top of intro bda1d87f694d via git's 3-way merge. Vulnerability (BufferOverflow): A heap buffer overflow exists in `sdf_generate_bounding_box` in `src/sdf/ftsdf.c`. Commit bda1d87f694dd replaced a correct `FT_NEW_ARRAY` call (which auto-sizes by `sizeof(*ptr)`) with `FT_ALLOC_MULT(dists, bitmap->rows, bitmap->width)`, which allocates only `bitmap->rows * bitmap->width` raw bytes. Since `dists` is an array of `SDF_Signed_Distance` structs (~12 bytes each), the allocation is roughly 12× too small, causing out-of-bounds writes on every access to `dists[index]`. Root cause: The programmer used `FT_ALLOC_MULT(ptr, count, item_size)` with `bitmap->rows` as count and `bitmap->width` as item_size to avoid the unchecked integer overflow in the original `bitmap->rows * bitmap->width` multiplication. However, `FT_ALLOC_MULT`'s `item_size` parameter is a raw byte size — not an element count — so the total allocation became `bitmap->rows * bitmap->width` bytes instead of `sizeof(SDF_Signed_Distance) * bitmap->rows * bitmap->width` bytes. A macro `FT_NEW_ARRAY_MULT` (which would accept a count and auto-derive sizeof) does not exist in FreeType, so the correct fix is to add an explicit overflow check and fall back to `FT_NEW_ARRAY`.
